messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT P1: hosted-runtime kvcache memory spike detected in us-west-2. Multiple backends OOM'd. Auto-escalation to #incidents and paging on-call.
Alice (on-call): ack. I'm looking. any immediate customer impact?
Ben (eng-runtime): I'm seeing kvcache.bytes_total jump from ~1.2GB to 18GB across several pods in the last 12m. Likely runaway prefetch + long prompt path. stack traces show OOM in kv_cache_store::append().
Carla (SRE): confirmed increased 5xx at the LB. 503 spike correlates with memory pressure around 11:03 UTC. Rolling restarts are triggering because pods exceed OOM score. TLDR: service partially degraded for some tenants.
Diane (Support): we've received 2 customer tickets (acct: zeta-ai, gladstone). Both reporting timeouts and partial responses. Escalating to CS.
Evan (Customer Success): pinged the impacted accounts and offered to switch them to our dedicated fallback endpoint. They want ETA to be honest — can we give an estimate?
Ben (eng-runtime): ETA depends on mitigation. Short term we can disable prefetch for requests with >16k tokens and turn on stricter KV eviction. That should drop memory growth within minutes. Patch incoming.
Alice (on-call): do it. Prioritize hotpatch over restarts. We don't want a full restart loop.
Ben (eng-runtime): opening PR now -> #4782. Patch: disable `prefetch_enabled` for hosted-runtime when `context_length > 16384` and set `eviction_watermark_mb=1200` for affected nodepools.

Ben (eng-runtime): snippet:
```
// runtime config change
kvcache:
  prefetch_enabled: false  # over threshold
  prefetch_threshold_tokens: 16384
  eviction_watermark_mb: 1200
```

Carla (SRE): recommend canary 10% first and monitor kvcache.bytes_total and OOM events. If stable for 5m, roll to 50% then 100%.
Alice (on-call): deploy-bot, run canary deploy 10% for 'hosted-runtime' with PR #4782
deploy-bot: acknowledged. Starting canary rollout (10%) -> ovens/hosted-runtime:hotpatch-4782. ETA ~2m.

(2m later)
deploy-bot: canary logs: pods 3/3 healthy. kvcache.bytes_total per pod: [1.3GB, 1.4GB, 1.2GB] vs pre-deploy [8.9GB, 10.4GB, 9.9GB]. No OOMs in canary.
Carla (SRE): looks good. promoting to 50%.

(10m later)
Ben (eng-runtime): 50% stable. OOMs subsided, 503 rate dropped from 4.8% to 0.4% cluster-wide. Prefetch-disabled path prevents runaway growth for long contexts.
Diane (Support): updated tickets: informed zeta-ai and gladstone about the mitigation. They reported improved success rates.
Evan (Customer Success): scheduled follow-up calls with both customers in 2 hours to confirm no data loss.

Alice (on-call): promoting to 100% now.
deploy-bot: rollout complete. All hosted-runtime pods running hotpatch-4782. No new OOMs in the last 15m.

Frank (PM): quick ask — did this affect Dedicated customers? I thought prefetch was per-deployment.
Ben (eng-runtime): only hosted-tier had aggressive prefetch enabled globally. Dedicated has per-tenant limits and did not exhibit this. We'll add better isolation.

Carla (SRE): collecting metrics for postmortem. Key things to capture:
- reason: prefetch + long prompt > 32k accidental; config threshold misaligned with token accounting in new tokenizer.
- impact: ~5 tenants affected, 2 support tickets, temporary 503 spike, no data corruption.
- mitigation: hotpatch PR #4782 + canary rollout disabling prefetch over threshold + eviction watermark lowered.
- remediation: add a kill-switch, improve observability (alert on kvcache growth rate), add preflight checks on tokenizer upgrades.

Ben (eng-runtime): root cause: tokenizer refactor changed internal token count heuristics (off-by-factor 2) which caused prefetch to request much larger KV ranges than before. Our `prefetch_threshold_tokens` default remained at 16k which now equates to ~32k real tokens.

Alice (on-call): handing off to next on-call: Carla. Key points in handoff:
- hotpatch deployed cluster-wide, monitor kvcache.bytes_total and OOMs for 2h.
- if OOMs reappear, disable prefetch globally: `curl -XPOST internal-config/disable_prefetch` (internal endpoint) or rollback PR #4782.
- follow-up tasks assigned to Ben: postmortem + tokenizer audit. Frank: prioritize customer comms.

Carla (SRE): taking handoff. I'll keep the channel open and will escalate to infra-leads if anything flares.

Frank (PM): adding note — need a clear comms template for regressions that look like runtime config mismatch. I'll draft it and loop in Diane/Evan.

Ben (eng-runtime): quick repro snippet for the team (dev only):
```
# simulate long prompt path
python scripts/send_long_prompt.py --tokens 40000 --endpoint hosted-us-west-2 --repeat 50
# watch mem:
kubectl top pod -n hosted | grep runtime
```

Diane (Support): marking tickets impacted -> "mitigated" and adding triage labels. Will follow up with customers after CS calls.

incident-bot: incident acknowledged, severity lowered to P2 while monitoring continues. Postmortem owner: Ben (eng-runtime). ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.

Carla (SRE): adding runbook item: preflight check that token counters didn't change during tokenizer upgrades; add alert `kvcache.growth_rate > 200MB/min`.

Alice (on-call): thanks all. Leaving channel, next on-call: Carla. :white_check_mark:
Carla (SRE): noted. I'll file the post-incident ticket and start data collection.
